subject: Anatomy
title: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All opens into coronary sinus EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Anterior cardiac vein ● Anterior cardiac veins open into the anterior wall of right atrium. ● Most of the veins of heart drain into coronary sinus except few like anterior cardiac veins and smallest cardiac veins. ● Smallest cardiac veins (venae cordis minimi, Thebesian veins) drain into all the four chambers of heart.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The coronary sinus:

options.label: A
options.text: Lies in anterior part of the coronary sulcus

options.label: C
options.text: Has venae cordis minimae as its tributaries

options.label: D
options.text: Develops from right anterior cardinal vein

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Ends in right atrium ● Coronary sinus drains the venous blood of the heart into the right atrium. ● Coronary sinus develops from the left horn of the sinus venosus, lies in the posterior part of coronary sulcus. ● Venae cordis minimidrain directly into the nearest heart chamber (drain into all the 4 chambers).

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Bleeding comes from the vein that is accompanied by the posterior interventricular artery. Which of the following veins is most likely to be ruptured?

options.label: D
options.text: Oblique veins of the left atrium

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Middle cardiac vein ● Posterior interventricular artery is accompanied by middle cardiac vein, which itself drains into the coronary sinus

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All are False about mediastinum EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: Heart is present in superior mediastinum

options.label: B
options.text: Heart is present in middle mediastinum

options.label: C
options.text: Thymus remnant may present in middle mediastinum

options.label: D
options.text: Posterior boundary of posterior mediastinum corresponds to T1- T4 vertebrae

questions.answerText: Heart is present in middle mediastinum
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Heart is present in middle mediastinum ● Heart is present in the middle mediastinum. ● Thymus remnants may be found in superior and anterior mediastinum. ● Posterior boundary of posterior mediastinum is from T5-12 vertebra. ● Lower border of posterior mediastinum extends quite inferior as compared with anterior mediastinum)

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: TRUE about attachment of suprapleural membrane:

options.label: B
options.text: Attached to 1st rib and its costal cartilage

options.label: C
options.text: Attached to 2nd rib and its costal cartilage

options.label: D
options.text: Attached to junction of manubrium and body of sternum

questions.answerText: Attached to 1st rib and its costal cartilage
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Attached to 1st rib and its costal cartilage; e. Attached to tip of the transverse process of the 7th cervical vertebrae ● Suprapleural membrane (Sibson’s fascia) attaches to the internal border of the 1st rib, its costal cartilage and the transverseprocesses of vertebra C7.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Compression of cervical rib can cause all except:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Thenar hypertrophy ● Cervical rib may result in thoracic outlet syndrome leading to compression of neurovascular structures such as the subclavianartery, the brachial plexus (lower trunk or C8 and T1 nerve roots). ● Arterial compression leads to ischemia, paraesthesia, numbness, and weakness of the affected arm, sometimes with Raynaud phenomenon of the arm. Nerve compression causes atrophy and weakness of the muscles of the hand and, in advanced cases,of the forearm, with pain and sensory disturbances in the arm.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Arterial supply of ventral 2/3rd of interventricular septum of heart is:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Left coronary artery ● Anterior 2/3 rd of the interventricular septum is supplied by the left anterior descending artery, a branch of left coronary artery.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Posterior interventricular artery is a branch of right coronary artery in most of the people (right dominance). In 10% population it arises from:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Circumflex artery ● In 10 % population, PIVA is a branch of the circumflex artery, which itself is a branch of left coronary artery (left cardiacdominance).

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: If the circumflex artery gives off the posterior interventricular artery, then the arterial supply is called:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Left dominance ● Usually the posterior interventricular artery (PIVA) is a branch of right coronary artery and such hearts are called as rightdominant heart. ● In 10 % of the population PIVA is given by the circumflex artery (a branch of left coronary artery) and then the heart is calledas left dominant.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Occlusion of the LAD will lead to infarction of which area:

options.label: A
options.text: Posterior part of the interventricular septum

options.label: B
options.text: Anterior wall of the left ventricle

questions.answerText: Anterior wall of the left ventricle
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Anterior wall of left ventricle • LAD (Left anterior descending) artery is also known as anterior interventricular artery and runs in the same named groove, supplyinganterior 2/3 of interventricular septum lying deep to it and also the adjacent anterior wall of the left ventricle. • Posterior part of the interventricular septum and inferior surface of right ventricle is supplied by PIVA (posterior interventricularartery). • Left lateral surface of the heart is supplied by circumflex artery.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which are segments of upper lobe in the right lung:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Apical, anterior, posterior ● Upper lobe in the right lung has 3 bronchopulmonary segments: apical, anterior and posterior.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is situated in the upper part of crista terminalis?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) SA node ● Crista terminalis divides right atrium into smooth posterior part and rough anterior part (embryologically). ● SA node develops at the upper end of crista terminalis, in sub-epicardial region.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All the following openings in the right atrium are guarded valve EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Superior vena cava ● Inferior vena cava opening is guarded by eustachian valve (rudimentary), coronary sinus by Thebesian valve and atrioventricularopening by tricuspid valve.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Torus aorticus is seen due to:

options.label: B
options.text: Aortic sinus bulging into left atrium

options.label: C
options.text: Aortic sinus bulging into right atrium

questions.answerText: Aortic sinus bulging into right atrium
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C) 
Aortic sinus bulging into right atrium
● Torus aorticus (aortic mound) is the prominent region of the right atrial septum, which marks the projection of the noncoronaryaortic sinus into the right atrial wall.
● The bulge is superior to the coronary sinus and anterior to the fossa ovalis.
● The right coronary artery arises from the anterior (‘right coronary’) aortic sinus; The left coronary artery arises from the leftposterior (left coronary) aortic sinus.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: In TEE (transesophageal echocardiography), which chamber is most commonly evaluated:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Left atrium ● Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) uses high-frequency sound waves (ultrasound) to make detailed pictures of theheart and the arteries that lead to and from it. ● Unlike a standard echocardiogram, the echo transducer that produces the sound waves for TEE is attached to a thin tube thatpasses through mouth into esophagus. ● Because the esophagus is so close to the upper chambers of the heart, clear images of those heart structures and valves can be obtained.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A bed-ridden patient on liquid diet develops aspiration pneumonia. Which of the following is bronchopulmonary segment is most likely affected:

options.label: B
options.text: Inferior lingular of left upper lobe

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Apical of right lower lobe > a. Posterior of right upper lobe ● In erect/upright posture (sitting or standing) aspirated material most commonly enters the right lower lobar bronchus andlodges within the posterior basal bronchopulmonary segment (no. 10) of the right lower lobe. ● Aspiration in supine posture most commonly involves the right lower lobar bronchus and aspirate lodges within the superior(apical) bronchopulmonary segment of the right lower lobe. It is found at the posterior BPS of the right upper lobe aswell.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Bronchial artery supplies lungs up to:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Respiratory bronchioles ● Bronchial arteries are the direct/indirect branches from the descending thoracic aorta and supplies till the level of respiratorybronchiole. ● They perfuse the proximal air conducting pathways including tertiary and terminal bronchioles and reach till the beginning ofrespiratory unit. ● Pulmonary arteries alone vascularize the further distal pathways, including alveolar ducts and the alveoli. ● There are pre-capillary anastomoses between bronchial and pulmonary arteries, at the level of respiratory bronchioles, thusstrengthening the dual vasculature of lungs.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: An inhaled foreign body is likely to lodge in the right lung due to all of the following features EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: Right lung is shorter and wider left lung

options.label: B
options.text: Right principal bronchus is more vertical than the left bronchus

options.label: C
options.text: Tracheal bifurcation directs the foreign body to the right lung

options.label: D
options.text: Right inferior lobar bronchus is in continuation with the principal bronchus

questions.answerText: Right lung is shorter and wider left lung
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Right lung is shorter and wider left lung ● Foreign bodies are more likely to lodge in right lung because, right principal bronchus is shorter and wider and more verticalin disposition. ● Right lung being shorter and wider does not count as any of the deciding factor.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which bronchopulmonary segment is absent in left lung?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Medial basal. ● Medial basal BPS may be absent in the left lung (Schwartz surgery). ● Medial basal is also called as ‘cardiac’ BPS of right lung.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Untrue about visceral pleura:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Supplied by phrenic nerves ● The visceral pleura develops from splanchnopleuric layer of the lateral plate of mesoderm, supplied by the autonomic (sympathetic) nerves (T1–T5) and is insensitive to pain.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The opening in central tendon of diaphragm transmits:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Right phrenic nerve branch ● Central tendon of diaphragm has an opening for the passage of inferior venae cava (at T- 8 vertebrae level), along with thatpasses few branches of right phrenic nerve. ● Aorta passes through an intercrural gap posterior to the diaphragm (T-12 vertebra level). ● Oesophagus has an opening in diaphragm (T – 10 vertebra level). Along with that passes the branches of left gastric artery and vein. ● Hernia common on left because of weak origin

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Oesophagus enters through:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Muscular part of diaphragm ● Oesophagus passes through muscular part of the diaphragm, surrounded by fibres of right crus and few fibres from left crusoccasionally.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Aortic hiatus contains:

options.label: A
options.text: Left gastric vein and thoracic duct

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Azygos vein and thoracic duct ● The aortic hiatus transmits the aorta, thoracic duct, lymphatic trunks from the lower posterior thoracic wall and, sometimes,the azygos and hemiazygos veins.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Structure NOT passing through oesophageal hiatus:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Left phrenic nerve ● Aorta and thoracic duct pass through the aortic hiatus, which lies posterior to the diaphragm. ● Azygous vein may pass through this opening sometimes, usually it pierces through the crus of diaphragm to enter the thorax. ● Greater splanchnic nerve usually pierce through the crus of diaphragm to enter the thorax. Right phrenic nerve passes through IVC opening whereas Left phrenic nerve passes through dome of diaphragm.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Secreting active thyroid follicles are lined by which type ofepithelium:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Columnar • Thyroid follicles are normally lined by simple cuboidal epithelium. • Actively secreting thyroid follicles are lined by simple columnar epithelium. • Resting follicles are lined by simple squamous epithelium.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Simple squamous cells line:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Blood vessels • Endothelium (blood vessels) and mesothelium (pleura, pericardium, peritoneum) are lined by simple squamous epithelium. Gallbladder is lined by simple columnar epithelium with microvilli (brush border). Ependyma lines the ventricles of brain and hassimple cuboidal (to columnar) cells with cilia and microvilli. Male urethra is lined by stratified columnar epithelium in entire lengthexcept the beginning (transitional epithelium) and the tip (stratified squamous epithelium).

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Basal layer of cell in stratified squamous epithelium is:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Cuboidal-columnar • The basal layers in stratified squamous epithelium are columnar, give rise to layers of cells that change to acquire cuboidal andeventually squamous nature, as they migrate towards the surface.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Lining epithelium of ventricles of brain:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Columnar • Ventricles of brain are lined by simple ciliated columnar epithelium and so is the central canal of spinal cord.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: In pemphigus vulgaris, autoantibodies are formed againstwhich cell adhesion molecule:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Cadherin • Autoantibodies are directed against the cadherins (of desmosomes) in pemphigus vulgaris, which leads to intercellular separation

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is a holocrine gland:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Sebaceous • Holocrine secretions are produced in the cytoplasm of the cell and released by the rupture of the plasma membrane, which destructs the cell and results in the secretion of the product into the lumen, e.g. sebaceous gland.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Sweat glands are which types of gland
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Simple coiled tubular • Sweat glands are lined by the simple coiled tubular epithelium.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Mucous glands are absent in:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Vagina • Vagina has no glands are seen in the mucosa, its surface being kept moist by secretions of glands in the cervix.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All cartilage is covered by perichondrium EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Fibrocartilage • Fibrocartilage has no perichondrium and has predominantly type II collagen fibers.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a hyaline cartilage:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Meniscus • Meniscus is made up of fibrocartilage.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Collagen found in hyaline cartilage is:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Type II • Hyaline and elastic cartilage have type II collagen fibers. • Fibrocartilage has predominantly type II collagen fibers.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The Haversian system is found in:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Diaphysis of long bones • Osteon is the fundamental functional unit of compact bone, which contains haversian system. • Each osteon consists of concentric layers, or lamellae, of compact bone tissue that surround a central canal, the haversian canal. • Haversian canal carries the neurovascular bundles to the bone. • Osteons are connected to each other and the periosteum by oblique channels called Volkmann’s canals or perforating canals.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following are categorized as secondary lymphoidorgans EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Thymus • Primary (central) lymphoid organs have stem cells for lymphopoiesis (bone marrow and thymus). They are involved in providingimmunocompetence to the lymphocytes. • Secondary (peripheral) lymphoid organs are in the periphery where the lymphocytes execute their immunocompetence, e.g. lymphnode, tonsil, spleen, MALT (sub-epithelial collection of lymphocytes) etc.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Subcapsular sinuses are seen in:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Lymph node • Lymph node is identified by presence of subcapsular sinus, containing lymph.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Cords of Billroth are present in which part of spleen?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Red pulp • Splenic cords of Billroth are present in the red pulp of the spleen between the sinusoids, containing half of the human body’smonocytes as a reserve so that after tissue injury these monocytes can move in and aid locally sourced monocytes in wound healing.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy -Thorax General Histology-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Follicles are present in which part of lymph nodes:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Cortex • Lymphoid follicles are present in the cortex region of lymph node.
